summary: Canadian Coast Guard light on the Saint John River at Gagetown, NB: first lit 1895, carried away by a freshet in 1901, present tower from 1934 after an ice jam.

lens.note: LighthouseFriends says the lantern holds a seventh-order drum dioptric lens built for use in Canada, citing a former Chance Brothers executive. Not verified.

structures.type: square wooden pyramidal tower with square lantern, on a cribwork pier
structures.note: 47 ft (14.3 m) from the deck of the pier to the vane (LighthouseFriends). Carried away by the spring freshet on 10 April 1901 and replaced in position. Destroyed by ice in April 1934.

structures.type: square cylindrical watch room and lantern on a square pyramidal wood skeletal tower
structures.note: Present tower. Height 9.8 m per the CCG list. Rowlett gives the watch room and lantern as 10 m (32 ft). LighthouseFriends describes a square wooden tower on wooden piles, 9.7 m (31.8 ft), with open supporting stilts.

access.note: Grounds open, tower closed (Rowlett; LighthouseFriends). Directions conflict: Rowlett places the station at the ferry landing just off NB 102; LighthouseFriends gives Route 103 and Ferry Road. The Gagetown ferry was shut down in February 2016 (LighthouseFriends).

events.note: Square wooden pyramidal tower on a cribwork pier, replacing the No Man's Friend beacon across the river (LighthouseFriends).
Fixed white light, 53 ft (16.2 m) above the water, to guide vessels between Jemseg and Upper Musquash Island and round the bend (LighthouseFriends).
Carried away by the spring freshet on 10 April 1901 (Department of Marine report for 1901). A temporary light hung from an elm tree.
Permanent light shown again on 22 June 1901, after the tower was set back in place. Rebuilding cost $268.73 by day labour (report for 1901; LighthouseFriends gives $269).
'Purvis, jr' listed against Gagetown, appointed 8 August 1903 (keepers' table printed 1904, page image checked). LighthouseFriends gives 'Jr. Purvis (1903 to 1904)'.
The original tower was destroyed by an ice jam in April 1934 (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett).
Present tower, dated 1934 by Rowlett and 1930s by LighthouseFriends.

keepers.name: Edmund Buzza
keepers.note: Listed by LighthouseFriends under 'No Man's Friend and Gagetown'. Those early years belong to the beacon that the 1895 light replaced; LighthouseFriends does not separate the two. Not verified in the Marine reports (the corpus holds none before 1900).

keepers.name: Morris Scovill
keepers.note: As for Buzza: LighthouseFriends' list, not verified in the Marine reports.

keepers.name: David Purvis
keepers.note: LighthouseFriends only. A 'Purvis, David' appears in the 1901 to 1903 tables beside Jemseg and Belleisle Point, which are not matched to this station.

keepers.name: Purvis, jr
keepers.note: LighthouseFriends gives 'Jr. Purvis'. The 1904 table lists 'Purvis, jr' against Gagetown with appointment 8 August 1903 (page image checked; the OCR shows only Aug.), position match on the printed row.

keepers.name: Fraser Fox
keepers.note: Listed as 'Fox, Fraser' at 'Gagetown, St. John River' in the report printed in 1908, appointed 22 April 1904 (page image checked). LighthouseFriends gives 1904 to 1912. The 1906 table (printed p. 260) also lists him at Gagetown with the same date.

keepers.name: Charles Brooks
keepers.note: LighthouseFriends gives 1912 to at least 1923. Not checked in the Marine reports read here.

corrections.field: structures: standing tower (9.8 m) has no build year
corrections.proposed: present tower built 1934 (Rowlett; LighthouseFriends says 1930s), 9.8 m
corrections.why: The brief's standing tower has no date. Rowlett dates the present station to 1934 and says the original tower was destroyed by ice that year. The 1895 tower was carried away in 1901 and replaced, so the 1895 structure is no longer standing.

resolved_conflicts.field: structures: first tower versus present tower
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 'first_lit 1895' and 'built 1934' both hold. The 1895 tower was carried away in 1901 and replaced, then destroyed by ice in April 1934. The 1934 tower is the present one.

LighthouseFriends describes the 1895 light as fixed white. The CCG list gives F G (fixed green) now, and LighthouseFriends and Rowlett also describe green. The date of the colour change is not given. The record keeps F G.
The present tower is 9.8 m on the CCG list, 9.7 m (31.8 ft) on LighthouseFriends, and the watch room and lantern are 10 m (32 ft) on Rowlett. The record keeps 9.8 m.
Rowlett places the station at the ferry landing just off NB 102. LighthouseFriends gives directions from Route 103 and Ferry Road. Both are recorded in the access note.

notes_for_editor: Moderate. The strongest records are the 1901 Marine report entry on the freshet (scan 79, printed p. 64; checked by corpus grep: elm tree within 20 feet, reopened 22 June 1901, rebuilding cost $268.73) and two keeper tables, both checked on the page images: 'Purvis, jr', Gagetown, Aug. 8, 1903, 80 00 (printed 1904, scan 229, printed p. 216; row aligned) and 'Fox, Fraser', Gagetown, St. John River, April 22, 1904, 80 00 (printed 1908, scan 149, printed p. 142). The 1906 table (scan 341, printed p. 260) lists Fox at Gagetown with the same date. LighthouseFriends is the only source for 1869 to 1897 (No Man's Friend and Gagetown), for David Purvis, for Brooks (1912 to at least 1923), for the 1895 construction details, and for the Grimrose and Monckton context. The corpus holds no Marine report before 1900. The 1902 table lists 'No Man's Friend' as a separate station; its keeper was not matched to a name, and the story names none. The Monckton campaign itself is not cited to a history here; the Grimrose account is LighthouseFriends' alone. The Chance Brothers lens claim is LighthouseFriends', quoting a former executive, and was not verified. Route directions conflict (Rowlett NB 102; LighthouseFriends Route 103). The present tower's description differs across sources (CCG: white square tower with a red top, 9.8 m; Rowlett: 10 m square cylindrical watch room on a skeletal pyramidal frame; LighthouseFriends: square wooden tower on piles, 9.7 m). No 'After the keepers' facts were found in the sources read (automation date and the end of resident keepers are not given), so that chapter is omitted. No wreck or rescue tied to this station appears in the sources read beyond the freshet and the ice jam.
